merger_description:
Itochu Corporation (**Itochu**) proposes to acquire an interest in the Aviation Capital Group business (**Aviation Capital Group**) by acquiring 50% of the shares in TC Skyward Aviation U.S., Inc (**SKYU**, being the holding company of Aviation Capital Group), from Tokyo Century Corporation, with Itochu and Tokyo Century Corporation to each hold an equal 50% of the shares in SKYU following completion (the **Acquisition**).

Itochu is a diversified general trading and investment company with interests ranging from raw materials through to manufacturing, distribution, retail, and services. In Australia, Itochu operates as a trading business across sectors including coal, metals and minerals, machinery, general merchandise, chemicals, and food. Itochu holds limited interests in the aviation sector in Australia, being an interest in Killick Aerospace (which has limited operations in Australia). Itochu is an existing shareholder in Tokyo Century Corporation, and accordingly already holds an indirect interest in Aviation Capital Group.

SKYU is a holding company for Aviation Capital Group. Aviation Capital Group is a full-service aircraft asset manager based in the United States which operates a business leasing commercial aircraft to airlines. Aviation Capital Group has approximately 300 owned and managed aircraft, which are leased to approximately 85 airlines in around 50 countries. It specialises in commercial aircraft leasing and provides aircraft asset management services and aircraft financing solutions to third parties. In Australia, Aviation Capital Group's services are limited to dry leases of commercial aircraft.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between Itochu and Aviation
Capital Group in the supply of commercial aircraft leases to
airlines in Australia
b. there are alternative suppliers of commercial aircraft leasing
services available to customers in Australia
c. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
or conglomerate effects resulting from exclusionary
conduct, bundling or tying of products or services post-
acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
